title: Season 01 is ducks. Here is what that actually means.
excerpt: One subject, three months, then the whole shop is replaced. How the quarterly model works, what happens when a season closes, and how the next subject gets chosen.
seo_description: Julia Mind runs one subject at a time. An explanation of the quarterly season model: what a season contains, what happens to stock when it closes, and how each new subject is chosen.

title: How to buy a bucket hat that actually fits
excerpt: Measure just above the ears, trust the centimetres rather than the size letter, and never size up to be safe. Two minutes of reading, one fewer return.
seo_description: A practical bucket hat sizing guide: how to measure your head correctly, what 56–58cm one size really means, the three most common sizing mistakes, and how a hat should sit when it fits.

title: Hanging a print without making the room look like a gift shop
excerpt: Buy bigger than feels sensible, frame it properly, and hang it lower than you want to. The three decisions that separate art from a poster.
seo_description: How to frame and hang an illustrated print: choosing the right size for the wall, why a mount matters, correct hanging height, and how to group prints without it looking accidental.

title: What actually gets checked before something goes in a season
excerpt: Four passes: does it belong, do the photographs hold up, is the description honest, and do the variants exist. Plus the things this shop does not claim.
seo_description: Behind the scenes of a small seasonal shop: how products are selected, how supplier photography and descriptions are checked, how variants are verified, and what the returns policy actually is.

title: Washing printed cotton so the print survives
excerpt: Cold, inside out, no softener, never the tumble dryer. Why heat is the thing that ruins a print, and what to do about socks, slippers and mugs.
seo_description: How to wash printed cotton shirts so the graphic lasts: the right temperature, why fabric softener and tumble drying damage prints, plus care notes for socks, slippers and printed mugs.

title: Nine ducks, ranked by how seriously they take themselves
excerpt: The rubber duck takes itself least seriously and outsells everything. The Christmas duck takes itself most seriously and is unwearable for eleven months. A field guide to Season 01.
seo_description: A guide to the recurring duck archetypes in Season 01 at Julia Mind — the rubber duck, the bucket hat duck, the cowboy duck, the wine duck and the rest — ranked, with notes on which ones last.
